newsitem.title: USA: Aronex plans multi-dose Zintevir trials.
newsitem.headline: Aronex plans multi-dose Zintevir trials.

text.p: Aronex Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Tuesday that, based on preliminary results from Phase I trials for its HIV integrase inhibiting compound, it was planning follow-on multiple dose trials of the product.
Preclinical studies have indicated that Zintevir inhibits the integrase enzyme, one of the key steps in the life cycle of the HIV virus, the company said.

There were at least three enzymes important in the replication of the HIV virus, the company said -- integrase, protease and reverse transcriptase. Drugs already existed to attack the protease and reverse transcriptase enzymes, but Aronex said its Zintevir was the first to attack integrase.

In a single dose rising study and a two-week multiple dose escalation study involving HIV-positive patients, results indicated the inhibitor, Zintevir, was extremely well tolerated when administered in doses up to 6 mg/kg, the company said .
